title: Jeremiah Chapter 28 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 28 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 28 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 28.

questions.question: In what year of King Zedekiah's reign did Hananiah speak to Jeremiah?
options: First year
Second year
Third year
Fourth year
questions.correctAnswer: Fourth year
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:1 states it was in the fourth year of King Zedekiah's reign when Hananiah spoke to Jeremiah.

questions.question: Where did Hananiah speak to Jeremiah?
options: In the marketplace
In the house of the LORD
At the king's palace
In the city gate
questions.correctAnswer: In the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:1 records that Hananiah spoke to Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.

questions.question: Who was present when Hananiah spoke to Jeremiah?
options: Only Jeremiah
The priests and all the people
Only the king
The elders of the city
questions.correctAnswer: The priests and all the people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:1 notes that Hananiah spoke in the presence of the priests and all the people.

questions.question: What did Hananiah claim the LORD had done regarding the king of Babylon?
options: Given him a new kingdom
Broken his yoke
Strengthened his power
Protected him from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Broken his yoke
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:2 states that Hananiah said the LORD had broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.

questions.question: How long did Hananiah say it would take to bring back the vessels of the LORD's house?
options: One full year
Two full years
Three full years
Four full years
questions.correctAnswer: Two full years
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:3 mentions that within two full years, the vessels would be brought back.

questions.question: Who took the vessels of the LORD's house away to Babylon?
options: Pharaoh king of Egypt
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
Darius king of Persia
Cyrus king of Persia
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:3 states Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took the vessels away.

questions.question: Who did the LORD say would be brought back along with the captives in Babylon?
options: Zedekiah
Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim
Hananiah
Jeremiah
questions.correctAnswer: Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:4 says the LORD will bring back Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim with the captives.

questions.question: To whom did Jeremiah speak in the house of the LORD?
options: Hananiah the prophet
Zedekiah the king
Nebuchadnezzar
The priests only
questions.correctAnswer: Hananiah the prophet
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:5 shows Jeremiah speaking to Hananiah the prophet in the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah's initial response to Hananiah's prophecy?
options: He rejected it completely
He said Amen and hoped the LORD would fulfill it
He ignored it
He accused Hananiah of lying
questions.correctAnswer: He said Amen and hoped the LORD would fulfill it
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:6 records Jeremiah saying Amen and wishing the LORD would perform Hananiah's words.

questions.question: True or False: Hananiah prophesied in the presence of only Jeremiah and the priests.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:1 states Hananiah spoke in the presence of the priests and all the people, not just Jeremiah and the priests.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah said the LORD should perform Hananiah’s prophecy if it was true.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:6 shows Jeremiah saying Amen and that the LORD should perform Hananiah's words.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 28, what event happened immediately after Hananiah spoke in the house of the LORD?
options: Jeremiah said Amen to Hananiah's prophecy
Hananiah broke the yoke from Jeremiah's neck
The LORD sent a message to Jeremiah
Hananiah was cast out from the city
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah said Amen to Hananiah's prophecy
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:5-6 describes Jeremiah responding with Amen right after Hananiah's speech.

questions.question: Which prophet is from Gibeon according to Jeremiah 28?
options: Jeremiah
Hananiah
Jeconiah
Zedekiah
questions.correctAnswer: Hananiah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:1 identifies Hananiah the son of Azur as a prophet from Gibeon.

questions.question: True or False: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took vessels from the LORD’s house and carried them to Babylon.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:3 states Nebuchadnezzar took vessels from the LORD's house to Babylon.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah condemned Hananiah immediately upon hearing his prophecy.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:6 shows Jeremiah initially said Amen and hoped the LORD would perform Hananiah's prophecy, not condemning him immediately.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 28 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 28 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 28:7-9, how can one know that a prophet is truly sent by the LORD?
options: When the prophet speaks of peace and his prophecy comes to pass
When the prophet prophesies against many countries
When the prophet speaks only warnings of war and pestilence
When the prophet is popular among the people
questions.correctAnswer: When the prophet speaks of peace and his prophecy comes to pass
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:9 states that a prophet who prophesies peace and whose words come true will be known as truly sent by the LORD, showing a connection with verses 7 and 8 that describe the types of prophecies given.

questions.question: What action did Hananiah take toward Jeremiah in the house of the LORD according to Jeremiah 28:10?
options: He took the yoke from Jeremiah's neck and broke it
He placed a yoke of iron on Jeremiah's neck
He prayed for Jeremiah
He rebuked Jeremiah publicly
questions.correctAnswer: He took the yoke from Jeremiah's neck and broke it
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:10 explicitly describes Hananiah removing and breaking the yoke from Jeremiah's neck as a symbolic act, which is key to understanding the conflict between their prophecies.

questions.question: What did Hananiah prophesy regarding the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar in Jeremiah 28:11?
options: That the yoke would be broken from all nations within two full years
That the yoke would last for many generations
That the yoke would be replaced by a heavier burden
That the yoke would never be broken
questions.correctAnswer: That the yoke would be broken from all nations within two full years
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:11 records Hananiah's bold prophecy that the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar would be broken within two years, which contrasts Jeremiah's later message in verse 14.

questions.question: After Hananiah broke the yoke from Jeremiah’s neck, what message did the LORD give Jeremiah to deliver to Hananiah in Jeremiah 28:12-13?
options: That Hananiah had broken yokes of wood but would make yokes of iron
That Hananiah would be honored for his prophecy
That the yoke would be completely destroyed
That Hananiah's prophecy was entirely correct
questions.correctAnswer: That Hananiah had broken yokes of wood but would make yokes of iron
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:12-13 shows the LORD’s rebuke through Jeremiah, telling Hananiah that his breaking of wooden yokes was temporary and he would impose iron yokes instead, indicating judgment.

questions.question: What reason does Jeremiah give in Jeremiah 28:15 for Hananiah’s prophecy being false?
options: Because the LORD had not sent Hananiah, and he caused the people to trust in a lie
Because Hananiah was not a true prophet from Gibeon
Because Hananiah spoke without consulting the priests
Because Hananiah's prophecy was too harsh
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD had not sent Hananiah, and he caused the people to trust in a lie
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:15 directly accuses Hananiah of false prophecy, emphasizing that he was not sent by God and misled the people with lies, contrasting Jeremiah's faithful message.

questions.question: What consequence did the LORD declare would come upon Hananiah for his false prophecy in Jeremiah 28:16-17?
options: He would die within the same year
He would be exiled to Babylon
He would be imprisoned for life
He would be forgiven after repentance
questions.correctAnswer: He would die within the same year
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:16-17 pronounce that Hananiah would be removed from the earth and die that same year due to teaching rebellion against the LORD, which was fulfilled as verse 17 states.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 28:8 describe the nature of the prophecies given by the prophets before Jeremiah and Hananiah?
options: They prophesied against many countries and great kingdoms of war, evil, and pestilence
They only prophesied peace and prosperity
They focused exclusively on the temple
They spoke only in parables
questions.correctAnswer: They prophesied against many countries and great kingdoms of war, evil, and pestilence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:8 explains that previous prophets predominantly foretold judgment involving war, evil, and pestilence, setting a contrast to Hananiah's peace prophecy.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 28:9 teaches that a prophet's message of peace is confirmed as true only when it comes to pass.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:9 clearly states that a prophet who prophesies peace is known to be truly sent by God when his prophecy actually happens, confirming the truth of his word.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 28:14 reveals that God has given Nebuchadnezzar power over nations and even 'the beasts of the field.'
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:14 affirms that the LORD has placed a yoke of iron on nations so they serve Nebuchadnezzar, and that God has also given him control over the beasts of the field, signifying complete authority.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 28:6 shows Jeremiah initially agreeing with Hananiah's prophecy and saying 'Amen' to it.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:6 records Jeremiah saying 'Amen' and requesting the LORD to perform Hananiah's words, reflecting initial hope or willingness to accept the prophecy if it proved true.

questions.question: Based on Jeremiah 28:7-9, what biblical virtue does this passage teach about discerning true prophecy?
options: Patience and testing the fulfillment of prophecy
Immediate acceptance of all hopeful messages
Rejecting all prophecies of peace
Ignoring prophecies about other nations
questions.correctAnswer: Patience and testing the fulfillment of prophecy
questions.explanation: Verses 7-9 emphasize hearing carefully and recognizing that only when a prophecy of peace comes to pass can it be trusted, teaching patience and discernment.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 28:12-14 teach about God's sovereignty over earthly kingdoms and his control over their rulers?
options: God places a yoke of iron on nations to serve Nebuchadnezzar as part of His sovereign plan
God has no control over earthly kings and kingdoms
Earthly kings rule independently without divine influence
God punishes nations by removing all rulers
questions.correctAnswer: God places a yoke of iron on nations to serve Nebuchadnezzar as part of His sovereign plan
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:12-14 reveal that the LORD has ordained Nebuchadnezzar's authority by placing an iron yoke on nations, showing divine sovereignty over rulers and kingdoms.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 28:15-17 illustrate the importance of integrity in prophecy and the consequences of false teaching?
options: It shows that false prophets like Hananiah suffer serious consequences, including death
It suggests false prophets are forgiven if they repent quickly
It encourages prophets to modify their messages to please the people
It shows that false prophecy has no real consequences
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that false prophets like Hananiah suffer serious consequences, including death
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:15-17 demonstrates that false prophecy is a serious offense against God, resulting in judgment such as Hananiah's death, underscoring the need for prophetic integrity.

questions.question: What practical lesson about trusting God can a believer learn from the interaction between Jeremiah and Hananiah in Jeremiah 28:6-13?
options: To trust God's word even when it contradicts popular or hopeful messages
To accept all prophecies that promise peace without question
To reject all warnings and only listen to encouraging words
To rely on human wisdom over divine revelation
questions.correctAnswer: To trust God's word even when it contradicts popular or hopeful messages
questions.explanation: The chapter shows Jeremiah initially hopeful but later trusting God's word over Hananiah's false prophecy, teaching believers to put faith in God's truth rather than popular or comforting lies (Jeremiah 28:6-13).

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 28:8-9 imply about the typical nature of God's messages through prophets and how should believers respond?
options: God often sends warnings of judgment, and believers should heed these seriously
God only sends messages of peace, so believers should ignore warnings
Prophets never speak of judgment, only blessings
Believers should reject all prophecies that speak of war
questions.correctAnswer: God often sends warnings of judgment, and believers should heed these seriously
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 indicate that many prophets have foretold war and pestilence, implying that believers must respond seriously to God's messages, not only seek peace but also accept warnings.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 28 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 28.

questions.question: What did Hananiah break off Jeremiah’s neck as a symbolic act?
options: A wooden yoke
An iron yoke
A golden chain
A silver band
questions.correctAnswer: A wooden yoke
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:10 records that Hananiah took the yoke from off Jeremiah's neck and broke it, symbolizing the breaking of Babylonian domination. This wooden yoke contrasts with the iron yoke mentioned later in the chapter.

questions.question: According to the LORD’s message through Jeremiah, what kind of yoke was Hananiah told he would make instead of the broken wooden yoke?
options: Yokes of bronze
Yokes of iron
Yokes of gold
Yokes of silver
questions.correctAnswer: Yokes of iron
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 28:13, the LORD tells Jeremiah to inform Hananiah that although he broke the wooden yokes, he will make yokes of iron. This symbolizes a stronger, more oppressive bondage under Babylon.

questions.question: What was the divine purpose of the iron yoke placed upon the nations, according to Jeremiah 28:14?
options: To make them serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
To free them from all kings
To unite them under Israel's rule
To prepare them for exile in Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: To make them serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:14 explains that the LORD put an iron yoke upon the nations so that they would serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, indicating Babylon’s divinely appointed supremacy at that time.

questions.question: How did Jeremiah respond to Hananiah’s prophecy regarding the breaking of Babylon’s yoke?
options: He immediately condemned Hananiah as a false prophet
He said, 'Amen; the LORD do so,' but also warned a word of caution
He ignored Hananiah’s prophecy completely
He joined Hananiah in prophesying peace
questions.correctAnswer: He said, 'Amen; the LORD do so,' but also warned a word of caution
questions.explanation: According to Jeremiah 28:6-7, Jeremiah initially agreed with Hananiah’s prophecy by saying Amen, but then he warned Hananiah and the people to listen carefully to another word from the LORD, showing a complex prophetic stance.

questions.question: What was the consequence decreed by the LORD for Hananiah’s false prophecy?
options: He would be promoted among the priests
He would die within the same year
He would be exiled to Egypt
He would be imprisoned for life
questions.correctAnswer: He would die within the same year
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:16 and 28:17 explain that because Hananiah taught rebellion against the LORD by prophesying falsely, he would die within the year, which he did in the seventh month of that year.

questions.question: Which other prophet’s fate is echoed by Hananiah’s death after prophesying falsely?
options: Uriah the prophet, who was killed for prophesying Babylon’s fall (Jeremiah 26:20-23)
Elijah, who ascended to heaven
Isaiah, who was martyred by Manasseh
Daniel, who was thrown into the lion’s den
questions.correctAnswer: Uriah the prophet, who was killed for prophesying Babylon’s fall (Jeremiah 26:20-23)
questions.explanation: The fate of Hananiah as a false prophet who died soon after prophesying falsely parallels Uriah’s death for prophesying Babylon’s fall (Jeremiah 26:20-23), illustrating the risk of false prophecy against the LORD’s will.

questions.question: What literary device is predominantly used in Jeremiah 28:13-14 contrasting the yokes of wood and iron?
options: Chiasm
Parallelism
Metaphor
Simile
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:13-14 uses the metaphor of wooden and iron yokes to symbolize different levels of subjugation and oppression, a common prophetic literary device to communicate divine judgment and sovereignty.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'yoke' in this chapter most closely signifies what underlying concept?
options: Servitude or submission to authority
A physical tool for farming
A symbol of peace and friendship
A crown or royal insignia
questions.correctAnswer: Servitude or submission to authority
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'עֹל' (ol), translated as 'yoke,' in Jeremiah 28:13-14 symbolizes servitude or submission under a foreign power, reinforcing the theme of political domination by Babylon.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of true and false prophecy seen in Jeremiah 28?
options: Matthew 7:15-20, warning about false prophets
Romans 8:28, about God working for good
Hebrews 11, recounting faith heroes
Revelation 21, describing the new heaven and earth
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 7:15-20, warning about false prophets
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:15-20 warns about false prophets who come in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravening wolves, paralleling Jeremiah 28’s concern about Hananiah’s false prophecy and its consequences.

questions.question: What historical context underlies the prophecy about the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar in Jeremiah 28?
options: The Babylonian exile and domination of Judah in the 6th century BCE
The Assyrian conquest of Israel
The Roman occupation of Judea
The Egyptian captivity during the time of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: The Babylonian exile and domination of Judah in the 6th century BCE
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:14 reflects the historical reality of Babylonian dominance over Judah during the 6th century BCE exile, a critical period of Israel’s history when Nebuchadnezzar ruled.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 28 develop the theme of obedience versus rebellion seen earlier in Jeremiah’s ministry?
options: By contrasting Hananiah’s rebellious false prophecy with Jeremiah’s faithful warnings
By showing Jeremiah joining Hananiah in rebellion
By celebrating Hananiah’s prophecy as the true word
By ignoring the theme entirely
questions.correctAnswer: By contrasting Hananiah’s rebellious false prophecy with Jeremiah’s faithful warnings
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:15-16 demonstrates the contrast between Jeremiah’s obedience to God and Hananiah’s rebellion in prophesying peace falsely, continuing the major theme of obedience versus rebellion in Jeremiah’s ministry.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage similarly uses the metaphor of a yoke to symbolize submission to foreign powers?
options: Isaiah 10:27, where the yoke is broken
Genesis 1:1, Creation narrative
Exodus 20:12, the Ten Commandments
Psalm 23, the Lord as shepherd
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 10:27, where the yoke is broken
questions.explanation: Isaiah 10:27 speaks of the yoke being broken from the neck of the people, similar to the imagery in Jeremiah 28:10-14, connecting the prophetic theme of deliverance and bondage.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah initially accepted Hananiah’s prophecy without any reservation.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:6-7 shows that although Jeremiah said 'Amen' to Hananiah’s prophecy, he immediately followed with a warning and a word from the LORD that challenged Hananiah’s message, indicating Jeremiah’s reservations.

questions.question: True or False: Hananiah’s death within the same year served as divine confirmation that his prophecy was false.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:16-17 states that Hananiah would die within the year because he prophesied rebellion against the LORD, and his death confirmed the falsehood of his prophecy as a divine judgment.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'beasts of the field' in Jeremiah 28:14 symbolize in the context of Babylon’s power?
options: The wild animals under Nebuchadnezzar’s control representing total dominion
Agricultural prosperity for Judah
The enemies of Babylon defeated
The divine messengers of peace
questions.correctAnswer: The wild animals under Nebuchadnezzar’s control representing total dominion
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:14 mentions beasts of the field given to Nebuchadnezzar, symbolizing his vast and encompassing authority over even the chaotic and wild elements, reinforcing his divinely sanctioned power.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 28 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 28 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What did Hananiah the prophet declare would happen within two years according to his prophecy in Jeremiah 28?
options: The vessels of the LORD's house would be returned from Babylon
The kingdom of Judah would be destroyed
Jerusalem would fall to the Babylonians
The temple would be rebuilt
questions.correctAnswer: The vessels of the LORD's house would be returned from Babylon
questions.explanation: Hananiah declared that within two full years, the vessels of the LORD's house taken by Nebuchadnezzar would be returned (Jeremiah 28:3).

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 28:5-6, how did Jeremiah initially respond to Hananiah's prophecy?
options: He said Amen and hoped the prophecy would come true
He immediately denounced Hananiah as a false prophet
He ignored Hananiah’s words
He prophesied a longer captivity
questions.correctAnswer: He said Amen and hoped the prophecy would come true
questions.explanation: Jeremiah said, 'Amen: the LORD do so,' expressing a wish that Hananiah's prophecy to bring back vessels and captives might come true (Jeremiah 28:6).

questions.question: What criterion does Jeremiah give in verse 9 for recognizing a true prophet of peace?
options: If the prophet’s word comes to pass
If the prophet is popular among the people
If the prophet speaks only good news
If the prophet performs miracles
questions.correctAnswer: If the prophet’s word comes to pass
questions.explanation: Jeremiah states that a prophet of peace is known as truly sent by the LORD when his word actually comes to pass (Jeremiah 28:9).

questions.question: What symbolic action did Hananiah perform involving a yoke, and what did it signify?
options: He broke Jeremiah’s yoke, symbolizing the breaking of Babylon's control
He put a yoke on Jeremiah, symbolizing submission to Babylon
He gave Jeremiah a yoke of iron to wear
He removed his own yoke to show humility
questions.correctAnswer: He broke Jeremiah’s yoke, symbolizing the breaking of Babylon's control
questions.explanation: Hananiah took the yoke from Jeremiah’s neck and broke it, symbolizing that the yoke of Babylon would be broken soon (Jeremiah 28:10).

questions.question: What divine correction did God give to Hananiah after he broke Jeremiah’s yoke?
options: He would replace the wooden yokes with yokes of iron
He would be promoted as a leading prophet
He would lead the people to freedom
He would be given a longer life
questions.correctAnswer: He would replace the wooden yokes with yokes of iron
questions.explanation: God told Jeremiah to tell Hananiah that he broke wooden yokes, but God would make iron yokes for them, indicating a harsher captivity (Jeremiah 28:13).

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by His declaration that He has placed a yoke of iron upon nations to serve Nebuchadnezzar?
options: Sovereignty over nations
Omniscience
Immutability
Mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty over nations
questions.explanation: God’s placing a yoke of iron on nations to serve Babylon demonstrates His sovereign control over kingdoms and history (Jeremiah 28:14).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about false prophecy does Jeremiah 28:15-16 teach regarding Hananiah’s message?
options: False prophets cause people to trust in lies and are judged by God
False prophets are eventually forgiven if they repent
False prophecy is tolerated for a time if it brings hope
False prophets can prophesy peace without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: False prophets cause people to trust in lies and are judged by God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah declared Hananiah was not sent by the LORD and that he taught the people to trust in a lie, resulting in God's judgment and Hananiah’s death (Jeremiah 28:15-16).

questions.question: How does the narrative of Jeremiah 28 show the tension between human hope and divine judgment in the redemptive story?
options: Hananiah offers a hopeful but false peace, while Jeremiah proclaims the true, difficult path under God’s judgment
Both prophets agree on immediate restoration, highlighting God’s mercy
Jeremiah denies that Babylon will prevail, showing God's protection
Hananiah’s message is accepted by all as God’s truth
questions.correctAnswer: Hananiah offers a hopeful but false peace, while Jeremiah proclaims the true, difficult path under God’s judgment
questions.explanation: The chapter contrasts Hananiah’s false optimistic prophecy with Jeremiah’s faithful proclamation of God’s judgment, reflecting the tension between hope and judgment in redemptive history (Jeremiah 28:11, 28:16).

questions.question: What synthesis theological insight emerges from combining Jeremiah 28:8 and 28:9 about the nature of prophetic ministry?
options: True prophets often prophesy judgment but are authenticated when their peaceful words come to pass
All prophets only predict war and pestilence
Only prophets who predict peace are true
Prophets never predict future events accurately
questions.correctAnswer: True prophets often prophesy judgment but are authenticated when their peaceful words come to pass
questions.explanation: Verse 8 explains prophets often prophesied war and pestilence, while verse 9 states a prophet of peace is known when his word comes true, highlighting the mixed but verifiable nature of prophecy.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 28:1 reveal about the historical context of this chapter and its theological significance?
options: It takes place early in King Zedekiah's reign, a time of political crisis and impending judgment
It occurs during King David’s reign, marking a time of peace
It is set during the Babylonian exile's end, signifying restoration
It happens during Solomon’s temple dedication
questions.correctAnswer: It takes place early in King Zedekiah's reign, a time of political crisis and impending judgment
questions.explanation: The chapter opens in the fourth year of Zedekiah, highlighting the historical moment of Judah’s last days before Babylonian exile—crucial for understanding the prophetic warnings (Jeremiah 28:1).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Jeremiah 28:3 and 28:4 convey about God’s plan for Israel’s captivity and restoration?
options: God promises eventual restoration of both the temple vessels and the captives from Babylon
God declares permanent exile with no hope of return
God allows captivity but forbids any restoration
God’s plan is to destroy all Judah’s leaders
questions.correctAnswer: God promises eventual restoration of both the temple vessels and the captives from Babylon
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 4 together affirm God's promise to bring back the temple vessels and Jeconiah with captives, showing His redemptive plan despite judgment (Jeremiah 28:3-4).

questions.question: What does the death of Hananiah in Jeremiah 28:17 demonstrate about God’s justice and the consequences of false prophecy?
options: God swiftly executes judgment on false prophets who lead people astray
False prophets are always rewarded
Prophets’ deaths are unrelated to their messages
God extends mercy indefinitely to false prophets
questions.correctAnswer: God swiftly executes judgment on false prophets who lead people astray
questions.explanation: Hananiah’s death in the same year shows God's immediate and just punishment for false prophecy that encouraged rebellion against Him (Jeremiah 28:16-17).

questions.question: From an apologetic perspective: Sceptics claim that prophecies of peace by false prophets prove that prophecy is unreliable. What does Jeremiah 28:9 and 28:15-16 teach about this objection?
options: True prophecy is authenticated by fulfillment; false prophecy leads to divine judgment
All prophecies of peace are false
Prophecy does not require fulfillment to be valid
False prophets are never punished
questions.correctAnswer: True prophecy is authenticated by fulfillment; false prophecy leads to divine judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 28:9 teaches that true prophets are known by fulfilled words, while 28:15-16 shows false prophets are judged, answering sceptics that prophecy’s reliability rests on fulfillment and divine justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is illustrated by God’s statement in Jeremiah 28:14 that He has given Nebuchadnezzar 'the beasts of the field also'?
options: God’s universal dominion over creation
God’s partiality toward Israel
God’s silence in political affairs
God’s withdrawal from earthly kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: God’s universal dominion over creation
questions.explanation: The mention of giving Nebuchadnezzar the beasts of the field indicates God’s comprehensive rule over all creation, not just humans or nations (Jeremiah 28:14).

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 28 illustrate the doctrine of human responsibility in relation to divine sovereignty?
options: Hananiah was responsible for false prophecy despite God's sovereign judgment
God forces people to prophesy falsehoods
Humans have no role in prophecy
Divine sovereignty removes all human accountability
questions.correctAnswer: Hananiah was responsible for false prophecy despite God's sovereign judgment
questions.explanation: The chapter shows that although God sovereignly judges, Hananiah is held accountable for teaching lies and leading rebellion, demonstrating human responsibility (Jeremiah 28:15-16).
